steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: Susan? Susan! Do you hear me? The enemy has heavy weapons not mentioned in the intel. We need fire support!

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: Susan! Where are you—damn.

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: We shouldn't have chased them here. How could they have a weapon like that... I knew nothing good would come of getting on their bad side!

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: We can still make it out of here! F-Forget the goods! Run!

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: Get down, you idiot! Stay in cover!

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: Panicking won't do any good. Stay put while I think of something...

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Stick close to me, guys! I'll provide support!

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Don't give up! We've come this far! Take back the goods, and we'll make it back in time to book dinner at the fanciest restaurant!

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: We won't live to see dinner if this goes poorly!

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Mom always told me that running away is the surest way to lose! There aren't that many of them! We can beat 'em if we work together!

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: I'll cheer you guys on!

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: Now's not the time for that! Their supply station is over there. We might be able to hit it if we changed position...

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: The enemy bombardment is easing up? Now's our chance! Get the others, Myrtle... Myrtle? Where are you?

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: What... what are you doing?

steps.name: Bandit Boss
steps.text: What? Why'd you stop?

steps.name: Bandit
steps.text: Boss, look over there... something's not right...

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Susan... are you full yet?

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Yeah, I'm full. Oh... you can have this roasted leg.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Thanks!

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Just don't choke on it...

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: We got five days off after completing that mission. You can eat here every day.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: And I'm not gonna waste a single one— Oh yeah!

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: So I found this on my desk this morning. It says... er... 'Field Operator Mission Report Form'...

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Do you know what it is?

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: You didn't submit your mission report? It's your first mission. Didn't anyone tell you?

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Mission report... I think I saw something like that, but I didn't know where to fill it out, and then I just forgot about it.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: So this is where I write my report? I just fill it in and submit it, right?

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Yup.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Easy-peasy! I'll do it right now.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Here, napkin. Wipe your hands first.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Let's get the dishes, Hoger.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Susan! I'm done!

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Wow, that was quick!

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Piece of cake!

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Let's see... 'mission complete'... wait, that's it?

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: 'Report—Mission complete.' Is there a problem?

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: ...Myrtle, are you sure you know what a mission report is?

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Of course do. When I was helping out at the mead store back home, I would write 'All checked' after I'd received and checked all the goods.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: But it was such a bother to write that every time, so I replaced it with a tick whenever I checked off an item.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Wasn't that smart?

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: ...Let me explain.

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: You have to write down what you did during the mission and your thoughts on it. Otherwise, it's just a piece of paper.

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: The mission report is submitted to HR, and then to your supervisor. It's a very important part of our work. You need to take it seriously.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: What? That's such a pain!

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Fine, I'll fill in all the blanks.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Code name: Myrtle... Combat experience... When I was five, I beat up a drunkard causing trouble on First Avenue...

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: You don't need to go that far back... I just sent you a template, okay? You can follow it and fill out the first few sections.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Great! That makes it so much easier!

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Hey, Hoger, wasn't the mission report due yesterday?

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: You're right! I remember I got it in just before the deadline!

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Okay, Susan, I'm done. Can you check for me—oh!

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Do you mean... it's too late to submit it?

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Let me think... I think the reports are still being processed at HR.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: I missed something so important on my first mission... Will I fail my trial period?

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Calm down, Myrtle.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Is there any other way? Can I sneak into HR?

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: S-Sneak in? Er... Hoger, you know a bunch of folks in HR. Do you know how long it usually takes for them to process this stuff?

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: Two or three days, I think. They're probably still... Hey, you don't mean—

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Just slip it into the pile and no one's the wiser.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: So I can sneak in then?

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: But that's against the rules...

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: I remember now! The operator's manual says you have to submit a mission report, but it doesn't say when!

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: We wouldn't have had to deal with this if you'd just remembered that earlier.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Whew... Now I don't feel so anxious.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: It's too soon to relax. You need to fill it out ASAP and sneak it into the pile before they're all taken away!

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: We'll help you recall what happened on the mission and finish the report, okay?

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: O-Okay. I guess it's pretty serious.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Let's start from the beginning. Do you still remember?

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Of course! We went into the barrens with that caravan. Our mission was to escort it to the destination.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Good. Write that down. Next?

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Well... the sun was hot and the air was dry. I was thinking I should put on more sunscreen the next time—

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: You don't need to put in anything that doesn't have to do with the mission!

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: Alright, how about this? Just write down what I say.

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: There was nothing out of the ordinary during the first half of the escort mission, aside from a few wild animal attacks.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Got it.

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: At 1604 hours... don't forget the zero.

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: At 1604 hours, we encountered bandits in the wilderness. I was responsible for protecting the caravan and providing combat support.

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: During the fighting, I made the decision to unload the goods from the trucks, which helped repel a wave of enemies.

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: Done? Let me see.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Here you go.

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: 'And then I accidentally chased the enemy away...' That's totally different from what I said!

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Nice and simple, isn't it? Exactly as it happened.

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: Just that? But I saw you...

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Yeah, I was protecting those guys.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: While you were fighting over there, I saw a bunch of people coming from the other side.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: A good generalissimo knows when to fight and when to retreat, so I called for them to get onto the trucks so that they could get out of there.

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: Then you unloaded the goods...

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Less weight means more speed, right?

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: ...So it was just an accident?

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: Should we put it in like she said, Susan?

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: I guess we could, but...

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: You should think about how the accident had the effect it did. That's why we write reports, after all.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: I have to put that in even if I didn't think about it?

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Reports aren't just to let others know how we do things, or for command personnel to reference. They're for self-reflection too.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: In cases like this, we should consider the situation, weigh the pros and cons, find a solution, and put it into action. Mission reports are about writing down what you were thinking at the time.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: And if you weren't thinking, you should organize your thoughts now, in the report.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: I see. So since there's a thought behind every action, and I should think about it now if I wasn't thinking during the mission?

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Correct.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Can I try to fill out the rest myself?

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: Sure. I'll look over it once you're done.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Hoger, there's something I need to check with you.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: The part where we chased the bandits back to their hideout and took the goods back... I was acting separately from you two at the time.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: You were fighting the bandits at close range while I provided fire support from above.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: We'd better cross-check the parts that I'm not entirely sure about, so that we can keep Myrtle... focused.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: I remember that! We started fighting at the entrance of their base!

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: I wanted to lead the charge, but it was my first time seeing a battlefield like that, so all I could do was get the others to cover.

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: That was more than enough.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: We had the advantage until they brought out some big thing, like, THIS big, that blew up a truck with one shot!

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: We would've been blown up too, if you hadn't pull us into cover!

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: There was no intel about any heavy weapons. It might have been a recent acquisition.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: I heard you talking about it over the comms. There was a lot of smoke and I was busy calibrating the distance, so I didn't really see what was happening.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: I was wondering, though... How did the two of you charge into the fray under that kind of firepower?

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: What did you do, Hoger?

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: I-It wasn't me. It was Myrtle...

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: It was all thanks to Hoger! He was amazing!

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: I saw it with my own eyes!

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Hoger leapt out of cover and charged forward with a war cry, and everyone else followed!

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: The bandits must've been shocked, because they just stood there motionless! It was like they were under a spell!

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: So Hoger just punched the guy, and down he went!

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Hey, why are you guys so quiet?

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: I remember it all so clearly! I'm gonna write it down now.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Hoger...

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: Myrtle, don't you remember what you did?

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Me? I just did what you asked, keeping everyone safe and supporting them as much as I can. Last but not least—

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: I gave everyone a morale boost, like a generalissimo should!

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: It may have been my first mission, but I'm really good at that!

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: I-Is that all?

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Yeah!

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: ...That's not how it went. Wasn't it all thanks to you that we won?

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Oh, stop teasing me, Hoger. Mom always told me not to take credit for something I didn't do.

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: This is how it happened, Susan:

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: Myrtle ran up to the front and jumped up on the ATV we were using for cover. Then...

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: ...She raised her white flag high and waved it. Everybody could see it clearly.

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: I was freaking out and trying to pull her down when I realized... it wasn't just us. The enemy was dumbfounded too.

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: So I took the opportunity to charge in while they weren't shooting. The rest went as she described.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Oh yeah, I was waving my flag! Haha, forgot about that.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Well, it was nothing. It's the generalissimo's job to keep up morale!

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: People always feel energized whenever they look at me! It always worked when I did it at home, anyway!

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: That's it?

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Yeah. To get something done, we all have to come together. We can do it if we work together!

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: And there I was, wondering how you came up with the idea of waving a white flag...

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Sounds like it had an unexpected effect again. I think I know what to put in the report now...

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: What are you going to write?

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: My reflections, of course.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: 'Sometimes my actions have effects that I don't expect, but my teammates always take the opportunity to defeat the enemy.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Therefore, I need to trust the people behind me and do everything I can to support them...'

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: How's that?

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Myrtle...

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: What do you think, Hoger? It does make sense, but I feel like it could lead to the wrong conclusions.

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: ...Let's see the rest of it first.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: My hand hurts... is this good enough?

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Yeah, I guess it's presentable.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Well, that was exhausting, but now I understand how you guys work! Very productive!

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Are you sure you really understand?

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Of course! Now comes the exciting part!

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Did you take a look, Hoger?

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: Yeah, all of HR is in a meeting right now.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: I know the layout of their office. I think I can slip it in... My only concern is that someone might suddenly come back.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Myrtle, how about you wait for us with the report at the door to HR? We'll scout out the meeting room.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Don't let anyone from HR see you with it! The operation will fail if we're discovered.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: No problem, I got this.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Here we go.
30 minutes later...

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: She's not back yet...

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: Could she have gone in already?

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Impossible. You didn't even tell her where to put it... She couldn't have found another way, could she?

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: Shh, the HR folks are coming back.

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: Hey, Susan, look at what that guy's holding—

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: It's Myrtle's report!

steps.name: HR Operator
steps.text: Good evening, Susan! Did you need something?

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Hey, just got a question... how did you get Myrtle's report?

steps.name: HR Operator
steps.text: Hm? Why do you ask?

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Oh, well, er... we were on the same mission, and we submitted our reports a while ago, right?

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: So seeing you guys take out Myrtle's report in particular makes me concerned that there might be a problem... yeah, a problem.

steps.name: HR Operator
steps.text: Oh, there's no problem. But honestly, I was wondering that myself, because the Doctor handed this to me just now.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: The Doctor?!

steps.name: HR Operator
steps.text: The Doctor said something to the effect of, 'Next time, give the new recruits a little more time to submit their reports.'

steps.name: HR Operator
steps.text: Even though the submission deadline for the new folks hasn't passed yet...

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Huh? So we spent half a day on that for—oh!

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Thanks for your time—let's go find her, Hoger!

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: Hey guys! I'm over here!

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: I was looking for you. Where are you going?

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Myrtle? Where did you go?

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: I came back from the Doctor's office... Sorry to keep you waiting.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Why did you go there? And how'd you wind up giving them your report?

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: That's why I was looking for you! I ran into the Doctor on my way here.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: They asked how I was getting on, and I talked about how I hadn't handed my report in yet.

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: That was okay because the Doctor isn't in the HR department, right?

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: So they offered to take it for me, and I accepted. Since they're the boss, they'd get it in the end anyway, right?

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: But then I remembered that I had kept you waiting here...

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: And the Doctor let me grab some candies from the office!

steps.name: Myrtle
steps.text: So here's the candy. Don't be mad at me, okay?

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: *Sigh*... Give me one.
One month later

steps.name: HR Operator
steps.text: Thanks for coming over today. I wanted to talk to you about Myrtle's performance.

steps.name: HR Operator
steps.text: Don't worry, it's not that there's a problem. All the missions she's performed with you have gone smoothly. We just want to know more.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: ...I'd still like to know the reason you're asking.

steps.name: HR Operator
steps.text: Very well. There are some... discrepancies between her mission reports and yours.

steps.name: HR Operator
steps.text: Frankly, they don't even sound like they're from the same mission.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: ...Didn't she said she understood?

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: It's our fault for taking her word for it.

steps.name: HR Operator
steps.text: Also... she submitted a few hand-drawn pictures along with her last report. Take a look.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: ...Generalissimo Myrtle's Tactics Manual?

steps.name: HR Operator
steps.text: She seems to believe that operators who work with her should understand her tactical thinking. So she put this together so other operators could review it.

steps.name: HR Operator
steps.text: You two have spend a lot of time with her. Do you have any, er... questions about her?

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: ...Hoger?

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: Of course I do. Who doesn't?

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: I don't think it matters, though. She has a knack for making things simple.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: As far as I'm concerned, it's easier to just charge forward with her than try to understand her through those pictures. We can put our trust in an outstanding operator like Myrtle.

steps.name: HR Operator
steps.text: Understood. I have no further questions. Thank you for your time.

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: (Whisper) That was the right conclusion to reach, right?

steps.name: Operator Hoger
steps.text: (Whisper) I... guess?

steps.name: Operator Susan
steps.text: Excuse me... could we borrow Myrtle's Tactics Manual for a couple of days?
